title: Loops
summary: Use for and range(), accumulating a total, while with break and continue, and nested loops to build an even-number sum, a sum of inputs until zero, multiplication tables and a star triangle.

even_sum.summary: Practice 1: add only the even integers from 1 to 10 to total and print 30. Before that, check how for, range() and an accumulator variable behave using the examples from the slides.
steps: On each iteration the next character goes into letter. After A, B, C the loop ends and Done is printed once.
The stop value is always left out: 0 1 2, 1 2 3, 2 4 6, 3 2 1. range(3, 0), whose direction is wrong, is empty and gives no values.
A step of 0 gives ValueError: range() arg 3 must not be zero.
An accumulator trace table: each line is n, total before adding and total after adding. Each iteration carries on from the previous total, giving 1, 3, 6, 10, 15.
The question from the slides: if total = 0 is put inside the loop, it is reset every time and only the last value, 5, remains.
The starter code has only pass, so it adds nothing and prints 0.
Adding only when n % 2 == 0 gives 2 + 4 + 6 + 8 + 10 = 30.

input_sum.summary: Practice 2: read integers one at a time with while True, break when 0 is entered, and print the total. First check the execution order of while, break and continue.
input_sum.notes: You can also run python3 input_sum.py yourself, enter numbers one at a time and finish with 0. If you get stuck in an infinite loop by mistake, stop it with Ctrl+C (the Stop button in Colab).
steps: The condition is tested first and then the body runs. The loop exits when count becomes 4 and the condition is False, so you get Done 4. Without count += 1 it is an infinite loop.
The break example is saved as /tmp/echo_q.py and given hello, hi and q. hello and hi are echoed back with Input:, and q ends the loop with no output, so Done is printed.
continue skips only the rest of the current iteration. Only 3 is left out, and 1, 2, 4, 5 are printed.
The starter code does stop at 0, but there is no code that adds, so it prints Total: 0.
Three tests: 3, 5, 0 gives Total: 8; 0 right away gives Total: 0; -2, 5, 0 gives Total: 3. Check for 0 first, then add.

multiplication.summary: Lab 3: read a table number from 2 to 9 and print its 9 equations (Invalid table if out of range), then use nested loops to print all 72 equations of the tables from 2 to 9.
steps: For each outer row, the inner col goes through all of 1, 2, 3. 2 × 3 = 6 pairs are printed.
Starter code: the part that prints one table is empty, and the inner part of the full tables is pass, so after All tables: there are only 8 empty lines (one print() per table).
Solution: 9 equations from 7 x 1 = 7 to 7 x 9 = 63, followed by All tables: and 2 x 1 = 2.
Counts the equations. The valid 7 gives 9 + 72 = 81; the invalid 1 gives only the 72 of the full tables.
1 and 10 give Invalid table. The full tables come after the input validation block, so that part always runs.
Boundary value 9: 9 x 9 = 81 appears twice, at the end of the single table (line 9) and at the end of the full tables (line 89). After line 89 comes the empty line that follows the 9 table.

stars.summary: Lab 4: read a height from 1 to 10 and print a left-aligned triangle with nested loops. If it is out of range, print Invalid height.
stars.notes: The optional extension is to add, after an empty line, a triangle that shrinks: ****, ***, **, *. Think of range(height, 0, -1).
steps: end="" prints the stars on the same line, and the print() after the inner loop ends the line. *, **, ***.
The starter code prints only the prompt.
Height 4 gives four rows of 1, 2, 3 and 4 stars, and height 1 gives a single star.
Height 4 has 1 + 2 + 3 + 4 = 10 stars in total.
0 and 11 print only Invalid height.
A common mistake: writing the inner loop as range(height) gives a 3 × 3 square instead of a triangle.
A common mistake: writing the outer loop as range(1, height) drops the last row, giving only two rows.
